summary: The tab scroll-restore journey asserts a cross-tab inequality instead of an exact offset, so it can pass for the wrong reason or fail when both tabs clamp to the same scroll extent.
evidence: cmd/goosie/journey_p1_tabs_test.go:96-105 presses PageDown twice in tab 2 and waits for active.ScrollY() > tab1Scroll, comparing one tab's offset against a different tab's; the same test then asserts exact equality (== tab1Scroll, == tab2Scroll) at lines 121 and 132. The inequality oracle depends on page heights and clamp values, and it is the assertion that failed twice under machine load. Re-measured 2026-10-26 on 6071b8b: 3 failures in 45 iterations of -race runs (-count=5: 1, -count=8: 1, -count=8: 0, -count=24: 1) and in the -count=24 run the failure was the FIRST iteration of a freshly built test binary while the 23 later iterations each took 0.16s and passed - the failing one spent its 8.12s inside this wait, so cold-start load is the trigger, not random scheduling. Two candidate mechanisms were measured and dismissed: (i) surface.mergeEvent folding two PageDown presses into one - a burst of four bare pressKey injections with no wait produced exactly four pages (one page 432, burst total 2160), so at steady state discrete keys are not lost; (ii) scrollContentTo computing the target from the shared scheduler viewport while ScrollY is per-tab - in 20/20 -race runs tab 2's ScrollY equalled sched.Viewport().Offset.Y at both steps (432/432 then 864/864). Replacing the second press with a wheel delta made the test fail 30/30, which is registered on its own as GOOSIE-WHEEL-001, so the oracle stays as written and the mechanism that parks tab 2 at tab 1's offset on a cold binary stays unidentified.

summary: On nine real web pages Goosie lays out nothing, or paints a handful of pixels, and still exits 0 with an empty stderr - the user gets a blank window and the engine records no reason anywhere.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-001. Measured by testdata/live-parity.py against Chromium/Playwright at viewport 1280x1024, dpr 1, wait_until=load, screenshots viewport-only on both sides. Source: docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json (94 of 100 pages comparable). Eight pages have doc_height=0 AND ink_goosie=0 with goosie_rc=0 and an empty goosie_diag: apnews.com (Chromium painted 15,805 ink px), www.nytimes.com (68,129), www.japantimes.co.jp (17,749), www.reuters.com (13,145), www.etsy.com (16,539), www.newegg.com (17,467), www.zara.com (8,846), www.gov.vn (501,735). vnexpress.net is a different shape of the same silence: doc_height=691 but ink_goosie=32 against ink_chromium=301,440. All nine carry the identical label in the earlier run (2026-10-25T1630Z) as well, so this is not load noise; of the 6 label changes between the runs none is in this family (www.usatoday.com was LAYOUT_EMPTY at run 1 and LOW_COVERAGE at run 2, so it is deliberately not counted here). Offline probes on saved copies of the served HTML prove this is at least two distinct causes, not one: www.gov.vn reproduces with no network (curl-saved 192,815-byte document whose decoded text carries 11,859 visible characters across 177,201 body characters, served with 26 inline <script> tags) and ./bin/goosie -screenshot on that file yields rc 0, ink 0, while -gate -frames 120 reports doc_height=0, tiles_rasterized=0, zero_work_frames=120 - the frame path ran 120 frames with no document to draw. apnews.com does NOT reproduce offline: the same command on its saved 2,610,822-byte copy (70,685 visible characters) paints 763,855 ink px at doc_height=34,867, so the live failure of that page must come from the fetch/response path rather than from layout of the markup. (www.gov.vn is also the only page in this family whose corpus expect is 'static'; the other seven are 'js-revealed'.) Caveat for whoever investigates: style_passes and layout_passes read 0 on both runs, including on apnews where layout clearly succeeded, so those two counters are frame-window figures and must not be cited as evidence that styling never ran. Nothing distinguishes any of these from a page that genuinely has nothing to draw: the -screenshot path exits 0, so neither CI nor a user can tell. Not root-caused further - TASK-038 §4 forbids engine changes in a measurement task. TASK-039 SPLIT (measured 2026-10-26, docs/tasks/TASK-039-LIVE-PAGE-NO-OUTPUT.md §5.7): the family is six branches, not one. Three now have fixes on main - the refusal status line (branch A: a source that answers 4xx used to be painted as an ordinary page with no note), `nodeType` in the JS binding (branch B: a Sizzle-shaped `9 === doc.nodeType` gate that never passed, so the setup script died before revealing content; oracle BR-188), and uncaught-exception recording (branch E: BR-189/BR-190, so a page that broke now says so on stderr). Three stay open: branch C (missing Node/DOM APIs - `createDocumentFragment`/`insertBefore` completion), branch D (paced modes never install `setTick`, so `PumpJS` never runs and JS-revealed content cannot appear in a `-screenshot`/`-gate`/`-bench` run), and branch F (the corner ink artefact, GOOSIE-LIVE-006). The comparable-page count did not rise, so this defect stays open. One page in the family did move: vnexpress.net went from ink_goosie=32 (BLANK_OUTPUT) to 320,348 (LOW_COVERAGE) between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps - attributed offline on one saved copy to the CSS string-state fix, see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-002, and NOT to any TASK-039 branch. CORRECTION (2026-10-26, integrator): the vnexpress.net movement from ink_goosie=32 to 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps is real, but the sentence appended above attributing it to 'the CSS string-state fix repaired the sheet' is falsified by a direct measurement - see GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003: on vnexpress's own second inline stylesheet the eef92ae parser loses a tail rule that da68c5b keeps (marker ink 0 vs 14,400). The page-level improvement therefore comes from a different sheet on the page, and the branch is still open for this site (LOW_COVERAGE, coverage 0.441). Sweep 7 (build `741fdd37`, 2026-10-26) repeats the headline case exactly: https://vnexpress.net/ is `BLANK_OUTPUT` with `ink_goosie` **0** and **6/6** reference bands empty, at `doc_height` 752, while Chromium holds 284,839 ink px — i.e. the page still paints nothing and still exits 0. Same row in sweep 6 (ink 0, 6/6). TASK-047's DOM/jQuery boot APIs are aimed at this row; its acceptance number is this ink count going above 0, not a label change.

summary: A legal custom property name that begins with digits (--8e8e8e) is mistaken for an oversized geometry dimension, so the whole document is refused: cafef.vn gets no window, and the message names no property, no value and no limit.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-002. Reproduced offline with no network from a saved copy: ./bin/goosie -screenshot -url file:///tmp/cafef.html (217,170 bytes) exits 1 and writes exactly one stderr line, 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range' (the prefix is doubled). The live sweep labels it ADMISSION_CAPPED in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json; in the earlier run it was GOOSIE_CRASH, the same family mislabelled before the ladder put a refusal check ahead of the exit-code check. ROOT CAUSE, measured by bisection and not yet fixed: document -> 9 <style> blocks (dropping them clears the refusal; dropping style= attributes does not) -> block 8 of 36 rules -> one rule, '.box-ttdn .list .mdn .time { color: var(--8e8e8e, #8e8e8e); ... }'. The one-line repro is ':root{--8e8e8e:#8e8e8e}' and '.a{color:var(--8e8e8e)}'. The name of that custom property begins with digits, so the tokenizer reads 8e8 as a scientific number and then swallows the following 'e8' as a unit, producing a Dimension token worth 800,000,000; internal/engine/limits.go:239-241 applies MaxGeometry = 2<<20 (2,097,152) to dimensions and percentages, and the document is refused. A variant matrix measured on this host confirms the mechanism exactly: ':root{--8e8:1}' rc 0 (plain number, cap deliberately skipped), ':root{--8e8e8:1}' rc 1, ':root{--1e9e9:1}' rc 1, ':root{--8e5e5:1}' rc 0 (800,000 under the cap), ':root{--1e2e2:1}' rc 0, ':root{--abc8e8e8:1}' rc 0 (ident, no number token), '.a{width:8e8}' rc 0, '.a{width:8e8e8px}' rc 1 (a genuine dimension, correctly refused). Chromium, measured with Playwright on the same minimal document, resolves var(--8e8e8e) to rgb(171, 205, 239): a custom property name that begins with digits is legal and contains no number at all, so this refusal is a false positive that blanks an entire news site - renaming the one ident to --grey makes the saved cafef document render at rc 0 with 554,999 ink pixels. Hypotheses already disproved on this document: replacing every 7-or-more-digit number (including z-index:999999999) does not clear the refusal, because the trigger is an 8-character ident with no run of digits; and the document loads no external stylesheet, so linked CSS is not involved. Compounding the damage, the same coarse message is emitted from three sites - internal/engine/limits.go:226 (float64 overflow), :231 (non-finite), :241 (magnitude) - and none names the property, the value, or the bound, unlike :249 'CSS declaration limit exceeded (%d)'. CLOSED, re-measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 rather than accepted on the implementer's report. Fix is in the tokenizer, not the guard: internal/css/token.go now orders the U+002D branch as 4.3.11 (a hyphen reaches readNumber only before a digit, or a '.' and a digit) then 4.3.10 (a second hyphen or an ident-start code point makes it an ident) then Delim, so --8e8e8e is one ident and MaxGeometry stays 2<<20 (TestMaxGeometryIsUnchanged pins the constant). Live page measured on this host at 1280x800 with the two binaries side by side: main at 2ca7889 gives rc 1, no PNG, stderr 'goosie: goosie: build session: CSS numeric value outside safe geometry range'; the branch binary gives rc 0, PNG 84,760 B, 1,004,804 ink pixels. Mutation proof on the merged tree: restoring the old dispatch kills TestHyphenTokenKind (6 sub-cases incl. -webkit-mask and --a(), i.e. vendor prefixes and custom-property functions were also being mis-tokenised), TestDigitLeadingCustomPropertyRefusalMatrix (7 sub-cases), TestDigitLeadingCustomPropertyPaints, TestGoosieDigitLeadingCustomPropertyIsAdmitted (exit status 1) and the parity gate itself (fixture render missing, 84/85, exit 1). Restoring the old content-free refusal sentence kills TestGeometryRefusalNamesEverything (both branches, per-field fail lines) and TestGoosieGeometryRefusalLineIsWellFormed; restoring 'goosie:', err kills only the process-level oracle - cmd/goosie's two unit tests stay green under that mutation, which is disclosed rather than fixed, because the line an operator reads is what carries the claim. Left unfixed on purpose and still open in behaviour: (1) '+' and '.' still go straight to readNumber without the spec's 'check if three code points would start a number', so a '.' not followed by a digit is not read as a delimiter - consequence not measured, so no new defect id is claimed here; (2) the guard's non-finite branch is unreachable from any token the tokenizer emits, so its message has no behavioural oracle; (3) escapes inside ident sequences are still not consumed, so --\-foo is not the ident the spec describes (GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001 family). Registry: BR-192 (tokenizer dispatch, INT+PARITY) and BR-193 (geometry guard and its refusal message, SEC+INT) cover the contract; fixture testdata/render/css-features/11-digit-leading-custom-property.html scored 98.90% PASS, corpus 85/85 at average 96.16%, floor 84 -> 85, tagged-case ratchet 73 -> 75.

summary: A -screenshot run that gave up at its hard-coded 25 s deadline is indistinguishable from one that settled: same exit code, same PNG, no field that says 'not settled'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-003. cmd/goosie/drive.go:170 sets steadyDriver's deadline to 25 * time.Second, and :241 ends the wait with 'if d.settledFn == nil || time.Since(started) >= d.deadline' - returning as though the run had completed. Nothing marks the difference: no stderr, nonzero exit, or field in the artifact. Measured headroom on the 2026-10-25 corpus: the slowest Goosie render was 8.93 s (www.straitstimes.com), then 7.70 s (www.noaa.gov) and 6.66 s (dw.com), so no page in this sweep reached the deadline - the gap is unexercised here, not proven harmless. The harness had to work around it by timing each render itself and inventing a NOT_SETTLED label (testdata/live-parity.py classify, selftest case 'slow'); any other consumer of -screenshot has no such signal. Changing the constant is out of scope for a measurement task (TASK-038 §4), which is why it is registered rather than tuned.

summary: The parity scorer can grade a page 'OK' while Goosie's ink sits almost nowhere near Chromium's: coverage is an ink-mass ratio that rises above 1, and the positional score (worst_iou) is recorded but never consulted.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 - a defect in the measuring infrastructure, not in the engine. coverage comes from parity.score_regions (testdata/parity.py:279): goosie_total / chromium_total, so it exceeds 1 whenever Goosie paints more ink than the reference. 30 of the 94 comparable pages in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1656Z-4de0fca5.json report coverage > 1.0, up to 2.83 (www.w3.org/Style/CSS/, 1,306,325 Goosie ink px vs 15,209 Chromium), 2.57 (ebay.com, 1,228,884 vs 94,816), 2.32 (validator.w3.org). Worse, the label ignores position: among the 46 OK pages, 26 have worst_iou < 0.5 and 16 have worst_iou < 0.1, including en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam (coverage 1.547, worst_iou 0.001, 0 of 4 bands blank) and wiki/Cuneiform (1.972, 0.014). grep of testdata/live-parity.py shows worst_iou is written at :162 (now :214) and never read by classify - re-checked after TASK-045: classify still contains no worst_iou or pct_exact test, those values are only surfaced through MEASURED_KEYS (:155) and the per-row note (:269). Written on 2026-10-25 as: 'blank-band and dimension checks are position-sensitive, so LAYOUT_EMPTY, BLANK_OUTPUT, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH stay trustworthy'. That half is now falsified for BLANK_OUTPUT: measured on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2, a band reported blank can hold Goosie's line ~20px away (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), so BLANK_OUTPUT does not by itself prove content is absent. LAYOUT_EMPTY, MISSING_REGIONS and DIMENSION_MISMATCH are unaffected by that measurement and still stand. What is missing is a positional criterion that separates 'content absent' from 'content elsewhere'. Disclosed rather than retuned: LIVE_COVERAGE_OK = 0.60 and MIN_SCORED = 75 were fixed before the first run and never adjusted afterwards (TASK-038 §6.5). Sweep 2026-10-25T2045Z-ec0f7fb9 (100 pages, 93 scored) sizes the OK-labeled half directly: of its 44 OK rows, 17 report pct_exact below 50, the worst being www.target.com at 0.24, w3.org/Style/CSS/ 0.63, tuoitre.vn 0.84, plo.vn 1.96, nld.com.vn 3.6 and ebay.com 6.4 - every one of them 'green' in the label table; 28 of all rows report coverage above 1.0. classify (testdata/live-parity.py:222, at :171-212 before TASK-045 moved it) has no rung for 'measured, and the pixels disagree', so a page with 0.24% exact match falls through to OK as long as it has ink, no blank band and coverage >= 0.6. Any statement about live parity therefore has to be made in pct_exact, not in label counts, until a positional rung exists. Still open after TASK-045 (merged ca39672), but two facts changed and are recorded so nobody reads them as a fix: the ladder's terminal rung is renamed from `OK` to `UNFLAGGED` (testdata/live-parity.py:124, feeding LADDER at :140 and SCORED_LABELS at :147 and the exit code) precisely because this entry shows 'OK' was a goodness word attached to pages with 0.24% exact pixels, and every row now carries pct_exact and worst_iou into the markdown table and the terminal-labelled page list. The substance of this defect - classify has no rung for 'measured, and the pixels disagree' - is untouched: a page at pct_exact 0.24 still falls through to the terminal rung, it is just honestly named now. Consequence for the sweep series: label-to-label diffs across the boundary need the mapping `OK` (sweeps #1-#5) = `UNFLAGGED` (sweep #6 onward), and no committed report yet carries the new label, so the first table containing it will be sweep #6. Sweep #6 (`2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb`, source 9754fda4, first report in the new vocabulary) repeats the pattern under the honest name: 43 rows carry `UNFLAGGED` and **14 of them report `pct_exact` below 50**, the worst being www.target.com 0.24, w3.org/Style/CSS/ 0.63, aljazeera.com 0.99, baomoi.com 5.64, ebay.com 6.39, dw.com 16.47 - the terminal rung is still reached by pixels that almost entirely disagree, because classify still has no positional rung. Same sweep moves the two numbers the floor is measured on: 95 of 100 pages scored (floor 75, met) and a noise pass of 12 sites whose max |delta_pct_exact| fell to 4.64 with **0 label flips**, against sweep 5's 18.36 with 4 flips on identical-ish code - so the reference side calmed down, and GOOSIE-LIVE-008's reopen shows why that comparison is only trustworthy read from the JSON `build` block.

summary: The CSS parser's quote-tracking scanners never end an unterminated string at a newline, so Goosie swallows the rest of the sheet and paints it on the page as generated content.
The ::first-letter admission rule is written three times and the incremental-restyle copy has no oracle: gutting it leaves the whole suite green.
evidence: Three copies of one rule. internal/style/pseudo.go:37-56 (resolvePseudoElements) and internal/style/pseudo.go:91-105 (reResolvePseudoSubtree) carry the identical 'before/after/first-letter' loop and the identical 'cs.Content != "" && cs.Content != "none"' admission test; the third decision is in internal/layout/arena.go:498-512. The re-resolve copy has none of the comment that explains the first one (pseudo.go:47-51, why content:"" must still generate a box for clearfixes), so whoever edits one copy will not know why the other exists. reResolvePseudoSubtree is reachable only from internal/style/incremental.go:157, i.e. the hover/restyle path. No oracle covers it: test/layout/first_letter_test.go:246 TestFirstLetterIncremental asserts only WorkCounts().LayoutBuilds deltas (:279 must not change, :295 must change by 1) - that a rebuild happened, never what style or box the rebuilt first-letter got. Measured at 452b6c2: replacing the first-letter branch inside the reResolvePseudoSubtree copy so it admits nothing left go test ./... green (mutation M2 survived), which also breaks the [R-7] rule that every oracle needs a positive expectation. Not a user-visible defect today - the copies agree - so P2: it is an uncovered-code and silent-divergence risk on the path users reach by hovering.

summary: A global inline-layout float skip shipped inside the ::first-letter commit changes float layout on real pages, is not needed by that feature, and no test fails when it is removed.
evidence: internal/layout/inline.go:387 - 'if k.Node == nil || k.Style == nil || k.Style.Display == style.DisplayNone || k.Style.Float != style.FloatNone' sits in inlineInto's generic child loop, so it drops every floated child from inline collection everywhere. git blame: the clause is from 2f1519db (2026-10-25, the ::first-letter commit); the rest of the line is db4bedff (2026-09-17). It is not first-letter specific and the feature does not need it. Scope measured 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2 by deleting the clause, rebuilding, and re-rendering all 80 corpus fixtures at 800x2400 with both binaries: exactly one fixture differs - layout-features/05-floats.png, 51,447 px of symmetric ink difference - and the other 79 are pixel-identical. At the scored 800x600 viewport the same change is 162 px and the fixture passes either way, so make parity cannot see it at all. On that fixture at 800x2400 the parity numbers flip hard: worst_iou 0.6866 -> 0.0000, coverage 0.9813 -> 0.9474, blank bands 0 -> 1 (Chromium band rows 1055-1071 cols 20-460 holds 2,775 ink px; Goosie holds 0 with the clause and 2,289 without). Those numbers do not prove the clause is wrong: the line 'Content after the overflow:hidden container (should be below).' is painted in both variants, about 15px apart, so the band goes blank from vertical drift (GOOSIE-BLANKMETRIC-001), not from lost content. What is proven is that it is uncovered: removing it failed no test in go test ./... (mutation M3 survived). Decision owed by the owner: either add a float test that fails without the clause and say which spec rule it implements, or drop it from the feature and land it separately with that test.

summary: A 'blank band' in the parity metric can mean 'Goosie painted that line 20px away', not 'content missing', so the known-gaps baseline counts and TASK-027's band classification are not evidence about features.
evidence: testdata/parity.py:253-279 score_regions(): bands come from content_bands(cm) on the Chromium mask only, and a band is reported blank when goosie_count == 0 inside Chromium's exact rows. The IoU path dilates by one row (_dilate_one) before comparing; the blank test does not dilate at all, so a line that is present but shifted by more than the band's own gap registers as absent. Two measured instances on 2026-10-26 at 452b6c2. selectors/03-pseudo-elements band (457,475): Goosie has ink rows 437-455 and 483-498 and none between, and the crop shows the paragraph and its checkmark painted. layout-features/05-floats band (1055,1071): both the current build and a build with the float skip removed paint the sentence, about 15px apart, yet one reports 0 ink in the band and the other 2,289. Blast radius: testdata/render-known-gaps.json stores 5 fixtures / 10 bands and is the release-gate baseline; docs/tasks/TASK-027-GLYPH-COVERAGE.md 6 classified those bands by cause, and at least three of them are now known to be artifacts; testdata/live-parity.py imports score_regions by reference, so every live row inherits the same meaning of BLANK_OUTPUT. Fix direction, without touching any threshold: report a drift-adjusted blank - search Goosie ink in a window of +-band height around the Chromium rows and label 'shifted' separately from 'absent' - then re-classify the 10 declared bands from the new column. LIVE_COVERAGE_OK, PASS_AT, THRESHOLD and MIN_INK stay frozen; this adds a signal, it does not loosen one. MERGED STATE, re-measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 at fc15c19 rather than taken from the branch: score_regions_drift landed as a report-only second view; scoring the SAME 82 renders with main and with the branch produced ZERO field differences across all 82 fixtures (match_pct, status, blank_regions, blank_region_rows, coverage_ratio, worst_region_iou) and the summary stayed 82/82 at average 96.088% with known gaps 5 fixtures / 10 bands. On the corpus the split is 10 declared blank bands -> 9 shifted, 1 truly_blank (html-features/01-forms-complete.png rows 593-599: zero ink inside the +-7 window, nearest ink 8 rows away). Three mutations were run and reverted here, not quoted: drift window = 0 reddens the selftest case that expects a shifted band, window x40 reddens case D3 (ink painted 100 rows away) so the width is load-bearing rather than tuned, and redefining the OLD signal inside score_regions - instead of adding a side result - makes `make parity` exit 1 on the known-gap equality. render-known-gaps.json is deliberately NOT re-baselined to 1: blank_regions keeps its original meaning, so declaring one band would loosen the gate under cover of a reclassification. BR-187 carries the oracle (test/gatecheck/parity_harness_test.go:TestParityDriftMetricIsGreen plus selftest cases D1-D4); the ratchet was re-measured, not assumed: P0 tagged 19, P0/P1 tagged 69, unchanged, because BR-187 is P2. WHAT STILL KEEPS THIS OPEN: the drift column exists only for the fixture corpus. The live sweep's 25 MISSING_REGIONS rows are still graded by the un-adjusted band count, and TASK-042 could not measure their drift share because live-parity.py writes its PNGs into a temp dir and shutil.rmtree removes them when it exits (live-parity.py:679,688) - so the number everyone will ask for, 'how many of the 25 are displacement', is still unknown, and the sweep's own label for a whole-page blank (BLANK_OUTPUT, 1 page, vnexpress at 32 ink px) is structurally NOT drift: with page-wide ink below LIVE_MIN_INK no band can reach MIN_INK in any window. MEASURED ON THE LIVE SIDE (2026-10-26, docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat is labelled MISSING_REGIONS with 1 blank band at rows [98,119] while Goosie's total ink is 215,401 against Chromium's 216,818 - 0.65% less, over a 23,269 px document. A page that paints 99.35% of the reference's ink and is called 'missing regions' is exactly the confusion this defect is about, and live-parity.py cannot yet separate shifted from truly blank because it deletes both PNGs after scoring (testdata/live-parity.py:679,688). The parity-side split is shipped (BR-187); the live-side split is the remaining half.

summary: Render parity is only ever measured on one host: the CI parity job on ubuntu-latest fails 14 of 80 fixtures while this macOS host scores 81 of 81, so a green `make parity` is evidence about a machine, not about the engine.
evidence: Discovered while closing GOOSIE-PARITYGATE-001, from CI's own artifact, not from a local run. The last three CI runs of the job 'Render parity vs Chromium' all concluded failure: 39990406790 (2026-10-23), 40069270435 and 40107385303 (2026-10-24). Newest artifact (run 40107385303, job 120911782700, head c8cd80b, ubuntu-latest, playwright==1.49.1): summary total 80, passing 66, failing 14, errors 0, avg_match_pct 93.638 at threshold 30 / pass_at 90.0. Same corpus on this macOS host at e310f55: 81/81 passing, avg 96.09%. The 14 CI failures are html-features/02 89.9, typography/09 89.62, overflow/01 89.28, typography/06 88.78, layout-features/01 88.76, typography/04 88.65, edge-cases/02 88.37, colors/02 87.19, tables/03 87.08, edge-cases/01 87.08, tables/02 86.39, positioning/03 83.95, selectors/01 81.64, colors/01 80.33. Two structural readings of that list, both measured: 0 dimension mismatches across all 80 rows (goosie_size == chromium_size in every row), so the pages are comparable shapes and the disagreement is pixels only; and the CI pass band starts at 90.364 while the worst failure is 89.9 - the verdict for 17% of the corpus sits within 0.46 points of the pass line, i.e. the gate is a cliff, not a slope. Hypothesis, NOT tested: Linux font rasterisation shifts text enough to move those 14 rows under PASS_AT, because no same-commit A/B exists - CI has never run at the current head and this host never scored c8cd80b. Why it must not be waved away: TASK-036 turned the known-gaps baseline into an exact ratchet, so render-known-gaps.json (5 fixtures / 10 bands) is now host-specific, and on another host a shifted band becomes 'known-gap baseline is stale' FAIL rather than a silent pass; whether that actually bites on Linux is unknowable from the artifact, because per-region scoring did not exist at c8cd80b (grep -c blank_regions on that revision's parity.py = 0) and the report therefore carries no iou, coverage or band columns at all. Needed, in order: one ubuntu-latest run of the current head with --render --render-chromium, its parity.json archived; then either a per-platform baseline file or a recorded decision that Linux CI is the authority for this gate; then re-examine whether a 90.0 pass_at is defensible when the host spread alone can cross it. Separately, the same run's 'Race detector' job also failed, so BR-179's 'go test ./..., go vet, archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit' is currently unmet on CI for reasons unrelated to parity - unmeasured here, since the failure log for that job was not pulled. CORRECTION to 'needs a Linux host': module-graph questions ARE measurable on this machine via GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go list (that is how GOOSIE-LICENSE-001 was proven), but PIXEL questions are not - no container runtime exists here (docker, podman, colima all absent), so the 14 CI failures cannot be reproduced or dismissed locally, and the only route to a Linux render is a CI run, which needs a push the user has not authorised.

summary: The distribution-provenance gate could not pass on both build hosts while it read the host's own go list - RESOLVED in code by BR-194 (per-target audit, merged 0cefc1d), but no non-darwin artifact has ever been executed and CI is still not measured green, so the provenance of the shipped binaries is not yet closed.
evidence: Gate 8 (test/gatecheck/licenses_test.go TestLinkedDependenciesPinned) is the only evidence for the licence provenance of the shipped binaries, and it enforces two directions: every linked module must be pinned (:70) and every pinned module must be linked (:78-82). go list -deps is target-dependent, so the two directions contradict each other across platforms and NO allowlist content can satisfy both. Measured at 32e3409 on this darwin/arm64 host without any Linux machine, because GOOS/GOARCH are honoured by go list: `go list -f '{{if not .Standard}}{{.Module.Path}}@{{.Module.Version}}{{end}}' -deps ./cmd/goosie ./cmd/goosie-headless | sort -u` yields 7 modules (regexp2/v2 v2.5.2, goja, sourcemap, pprof, x/image v0.45.0, x/net v0.60.0, x/text v0.42.0) with no x/sys, while the same command under GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 yields 8, adding golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 (chain: go mod why -m golang.org/x/sys -> x/image/font/opentype -> x/image/vector -> x/sys/cpu; x/image/vector IS linked on darwin too - grep -c gives 1 - so the delta is precisely the x/sys/cpu leaf). Both directions of the trap were run, not inferred: CI's own log for run 40107385303 job 120911782481 at head c8cd80b says 'licenses_test.go:71: linked module golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is not in dependency-licenses.txt (re-audit and amend)' and that is the ONLY test failure in that job (no DATA RACE line anywhere in it, so the job title is misleading), while appending exactly that line here and re-running produced 'licenses_test.go:80: allowlist entry golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0 is linked into no release binary (stale pin?)' -> FAIL, after which the file was restored and the test went ok again. Consequence for the release DoD: BR-179 ('go test ./..., go vet -all ./..., archtest and the gate suite all exit 0 on the candidate commit') is unmet on CI for this single cause, and it has been unmet for the last three runs (39990406790, 40069270435, 40107385303). The licence itself is not the problem: /Users/vyquocvu/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/x/sys@v0.48.0/LICENSE is the standard Go BSD-3-Clause text (Copyright 2009 The Go Authors; three conditions including the no-endorsement clause; ALL WARRANTIES disclaimer), already inside the permitted set, and the directory's PATENTS file is golang's standard grant, not copyleft. What is owed is a target-aware contract: declare the release target list in code, pin the union of modules across those targets, and judge staleness only against modules absent from EVERY target - plus a table-driven oracle so this fails on any laptop before CI does. TASK-043 §2 leaves one thing unmeasured on purpose: whether a third target (windows, linux/arm64) pulls yet another module. Update 2026-10-26, integrator re-measurement on merged main (0cefc1d, registry 501d6a0): the contradiction is broken - the gate now resolves `go list -deps` for each of the five release targets and calls a pin stale only if NO target links it. The original diagnosis was also slightly wrong about the shape: golang.org/x/sys is not Linux-only, it is amd64-only (measured per target on cmd/goosie + cmd/goosie-headless: x/sys present on darwin/amd64, linux/amd64, windows/amd64; absent on darwin/arm64 and linux/arm64) - exactly the case a flat host-pinned allowlist hides. Mutation evidence: dropping the x/sys pin reddens exactly the three amd64 targets under the new gate, while the same mutation scored by the pre-fix gate at 6071b8b is rc 0 PASS, and adding the pin back under that pre-fix logic is rejected as a stale pin. What still keeps this open: no linux or windows binary was ever run here (no docker, podman, colima, qemu-x86_64, wine), the non-darwin sets are verified as dependency graphs plus successful cross-builds only, the pinned CGO_ENABLED=0 has not been reconciled against the real CI build environment, and CI has not been measured green because no push was performed.

summary: The TASK-041 bad-string fix treated every newline inside a quoted CSS string as the line break that ends it, including an escaped one (`\` + newline), so real stylesheets that split a long quoted value across two lines lost that declaration AND the rest of the sheet: doc.rust-lang.org/std/ dropped from 95,783 ink px to 53,215. No committed gate could see it.
evidence: Mechanism: f5cec79 (the commit that closed GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-001) added `closesStringAt(quote, c) { return c == quote || c == '\n' }` and wired it into three scanners - parseRule's selector loop, parseRule's declaration-body loop, and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop - with no handling of the backslash that escapes the next byte. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.7 makes a RAW newline end an open string as a bad-string, but 4.3.8 makes `\` + newline a valid escape *inside* the token. rustdoc's generated CSS ends five lines (6/54/61/65/68 of its main sheet) with `\` inside `url("data:image/svg+xml,…")`, so Goosie cut the string, ate the `;`, dropped the declaration, and lost every rule after it in that sheet. Ground truth measured on Chromium/Playwright 131.x on this host, four shapes, all in TASK-041 §7.1: escaped `url()` keeps 2 rules with `background-image` computed to `url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='a'%3E%3C/svg%3E")` and the image loading; escaped `font-family` computes to `GoosieSerif`; a RAW newline keeps 1 rule with 0 declarations and computed colour black; an escaped newline in an attribute selector yields 2 rules with selectorText `a[title="xy"]` and the following `.z` still applying. Pre-fix Goosie scored 0 declarations, 0 declarations, 0 declarations (already correct) and 1 merged rule respectively. Real-page effect, same canvas 1280x1024 dpr 1, metric parity.ink_mask: 4de0fca 95,783 px / 23 content bands, da68c5b (TASK-041 merged) 53,215 px / 16 bands, after the fix 95,814 px / 23 bands. On the minimal probe /tmp/escprobe/escaped-newline.html at 800x600 the fixed build's PNG is md5-identical to the 4de0fca PNG (c47c831b9f4889fa31eaa3ca127364f9) - green 40,000 / red 40,000 px vs the regression's 0 / 0 / 445 ink. WHY NO GATE SAW IT, which is the part worth keeping: `make parity` reported 81/81 passing at average 96.09% both before and after the regression shipped, because no fixture in testdata/render contained an escaped newline; the unit oracle in test/css covered four raw-newline shapes and no backslash; and a SAVED copy of the same rustdoc page renders identically on both binaries (51,939 px / 17 bands) because the escaped CSS only arrives on a fresh fetch - so the offline A/B that validated TASK-041 was blind by construction. The only thing that caught it was the 100-site live sweep (docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1845Z-da68c5bc.json), which is evidence for the sweep being a gate and not a report. Fixed in a9f6218: the three scanners skip the byte after a backslash while a string is open, and stripEscapedNewlines removes `\` + line-break pairs from inside quoted values the way Chromium computes them, leaving `\2014`, `\A` and Windows paths untouched. Proofs measured: (M1) reverting internal/css/parser.go makes the new fixture css-features/09-escaped-newline-string.html score 84.87% FAIL with blank_regions 2/0 rows [(295,310),(425,452)], 81/82 passing, parity exit 1; (M2) deleting only the stripEscapedNewlines call reddens exactly one assertion - and the fixture stays green at 96.24%, so the value-unescape half is guarded by the unit oracle ONLY, stated plainly rather than assumed; (M3) the raw-newline control branch of TestEscapedNewlineVersusRawNewline was green before the fix and stays green after it, so nothing was loosened. Still open in this family, recorded not hidden: escaped QUOTES (`content:"a\"b"`) still close the string at the five scanners this change did not touch (parser.go :1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), which is the same debt §6 of TASK-041 already logged for stripComments and readString; and Goosie keeps the escape pair verbatim in selector text (`a[title="x\<NL>y"]`) where Chromium serialises `a[title="xy"]`. BR-186 now carries 9 tests and its measured row names both defects.

summary: A Content-Type sent with a comma instead of a semicolon (`text/html, charset=UTF-8`) is not recognised as a displayable type, so Goosie treats the response as a download: the page never paints and -screenshot exits 1 with no PNG while Chromium renders the same bytes.
evidence: Found by the 100-site live sweep at da68c5b, on https://www.target.com/s/coffee (label changed OK -> FETCH_FAILED-class, then proven to be neither network nor a Goosie regression). Root cause: internal/download/download.go:21 ShouldDownload strips parameters with `strings.IndexByte(ct, ';')` only, so the header value `text/html, charset=UTF-8` lowercases to `text/html, charset=utf-8`, matches none of the four whitelisted cases, and falls through to `default: return true` - download it. RFC 9110 §8.3 puts parameters after `;`, so the comma form is a server-side bug, but a browser is the party that has to cope and Chromium does. Measured offline, not argued: /tmp/ctprobe/serve.py replays the exact response bytes the site sends (429 status, `Content-Type: text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, the challenge body); against that single server Goosie exits 1 and writes no PNG while Playwright/Chromium renders the body. Pre-existing, not caused by the CSS work: `git diff 4de0fca HEAD -- internal/net internal/download` is empty. Blast radius measured so far is one URL in the 100-site corpus; the shape is common enough (429 challenge pages served with a hand-built header) that the honest description is 'unknown until swept again'. What closing it needs: parameter parsing that splits on ';' and trims, a table-driven oracle in test/download covering `text/html`, `text/html;charset=utf-8`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, `text/html, charset=UTF-8`, `application/xhtml+xml`, and a genuinely downloadable `application/pdf; charset=binary`; plus a user-visible consequence - a -screenshot run whose answer was routed to the downloader must say so on stderr instead of exiting 1 silently, which is the same class as GOOSIE-LIVE-003 (a run that gave up looks like a run that succeeded).

summary: The parity harness reads and writes two fixed /tmp directories, so two agents or two worktrees running it at the same time score one run's renders against another's - and the collision surfaces as a traceback, not as a refusal.
evidence: GOOSIE = Path('/tmp/goosie-renders') and CHROMIUM = Path('/tmp/playwright-renders') (testdata/parity.py:59-60) are global, unversioned and shared by every checkout on the machine, and --render truncates them in place. Measured at 02:10 on 2026-10-26: while this session's 100-site live sweep and another agent's `make parity` (pid 87939, `testdata/parity.py --render --render-chromium`) were both running, a read-only scoring pass in a third checkout died with `PIL.UnidentifiedImageError: cannot identify image file '/tmp/goosie-renders/grid/02-grid-alignment.png'` - a half-written PNG from the other process, rc 1, no verdict. The crash is the harmless outcome: the same race lets run A's Goosie renders be scored against run B's Chromium references, from different binaries, with nothing in the report saying which build produced either side. TASK-036 already established that a green `make parity` is one host's evidence; this is the same weakness one level down - within one host it is not even one BUILD's evidence. What closing needs: one render directory per run (mkdtemp, or a path derived from the binary's sha256), the chosen directory recorded in the JSON report next to each fixture, and a selftest case that proves two concurrent runs cannot read each other's files. Note the discipline that follows for agents: TASK-042 deliberately ran `python3 testdata/parity.py` without --render to avoid destroying evidence that other work was reading (its rule 9), which is right but invisible - nothing in the harness says the directory is somebody else's evidence. Same root, one more failure mode measured 2026-10-26 while integrating TASK-040: a mutation that makes a fixture stop rendering at all (rc 1, no PNG written) leaves the PREVIOUS run's PNG sitting at /tmp/goosie-renders/<fixture>.png, and `--render` then scores that stale image as if the current binary had produced it. Caught only because the good PNG was moved away by hand first - with it in place the mutated binary still reported 85/85 100%. The MISSING/exit-1 half of the corpus gate therefore depends on the shared directory being clean, which nothing in the harness enforces. Fixing this is the same change as the per-run directory: render into a fresh path and treat any pre-existing image for a fixture as not-this-run's evidence.

summary: A document the source refused (4xx) is still rendered and scored as if it were the page, so the live harness labels a blocked site LAYOUT_EMPTY - 'the engine made nothing' and 'the site said no' share one label.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-005. TASK-039 put the refusal on stderr (`goosie: the source refused <url> with HTTP <status>; rendered <n> bytes of that refusal, not the page`, cmd/goosie/document_loader.go:455, oracle BR-190 with mutation M5 re-measured by the integrator: nipping the threshold to `>= 0` kills `TestGoosieScreenshotStaysSilentOnAnAcceptedDocument`). The harness half is not done: testdata/live-parity.py compares whatever Chromium and Goosie each painted and has no field for the HTTP status, so a 403 body scores as LAYOUT_EMPTY or LOW_COVERAGE. Measured in docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T1920Z-eef92ae7.json: 8 rows carry LAYOUT_EMPTY, and the sweep's own `goosie_diag` is where the refusal now lives, not in the label. What closing needs: capture the response status per page, add a REFUSED_BY_SOURCE label, and count how many of the current LAYOUT_EMPTY rows are actually refusals - until then the eight-page figure inside GOOSIE-LIVE-001 is an upper bound that mixes two causes.

summary: A 20-32 px ink smudge in the top-left corner of Goosie's renders is counted by content_bands as a content band, so a page whose only Goosie output is that smudge reads as 'has content'.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-006. At ink_goosie=32 the vnexpress.net render (viewport 1280x1024) is a smudge inside (0,0)-(4,3) and nothing else; parity.content_bands treats its row range as a band, and the sweep recorded it as BLANK_OUTPUT only because the coverage ratio collapsed, not because the band was rejected. TASK-039 §5.5 measured what the smudge is (branch F) but did not root-cause which tile produces it, and §5.11.4 records that the probe needed is on the raster/frame side with a minimal fixture. What closing needs: a fixture that paints nothing but the corner, a statement of which of the two (uncovered tile, glyph-atlas bleed) it is, and a floor in the band metric that ignores a band of that size - the floor must be set from measurement, not tuned until the label goes away. CLOSED by TASK-046's localisation (adf2664, merged in 9754fda) on a mechanism shipped by TASK-044 (9e08c9d), and by the integrator's own re-measurement. This entry asked which of two causes it was - uncovered tile or glyph-atlas bleed - and the answer measured on this host is **neither**: with `raster.RasterizeTile` on an empty list over a fully covered tile the ink is 0, and the tile raster of the real list is pixel-identical to the headless PNG, so the ink is authored in the display list. The shape is two zero-size boxes at content (0,0) - `.sub-area` and `.nav-folder .ul-nav-folder li.has-submn .sub-more`, both `opacity: 0; visibility: hidden` - whose `box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.2)` ring strips survive into the origin tile: 4 cols x 5 rows = 20 px, and the colour arithmetic closes (`255*0.8^4 = 104`, `255*0.8^2 = 163`, `247*0.8^4 = 101`, `247*0.8^2 = 158` - exactly the values TASK-039 §5.5 recorded). They painted at full strength because `DisplayCmd.Opacity == 0` is the reserved 'unset -> opaque' sentinel (`internal/paint/cmd.go:151-154`). The third closing condition - a floor in the band metric - is dropped as unnecessary, measured not assumed: `parity.content_bands` returns **0 bands** for the 4x5 smudge in both the pre-fix and the merged binary (5 rows < MIN_BAND_HEIGHT 6, 20 px < MIN_INK 200), so no threshold was added and vnexpress stays BLANK_OUTPUT for the reason GOOSIE-LIVE-001 owns. The band premise was true one shape wider: an `opacity: 0` element with a 40x40 background put **1600 opaque px** on the page and produced **1 band** before the fix; integrator's own numbers with two binaries built here (headless 800x600 DPR 1, `parity.ink_mask`): bg-op0 1600 -> 0, shadow-op0 20 -> 0, a *visible* shadow control 20 -> 20 unchanged, empty 0 -> 0. Oracle: `test/paint/invisible_box_test.go` tagged BR-196, and both of its suppression cases go red when the merged guards are removed (see §8 of the task doc).

summary: An escaped quote inside an unquoted url() token opens a string that never closes, so every rule after it in the same stylesheet is dropped - the shape that hides vnexpress's tail rules and that the current parser only survives by luck when the sheet holds an even number of quote characters.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003. CSS Syntax L3 4.3.8 makes a backslash escape the next byte anywhere in the token stream, so `\'` inside `url(...)` must not start a string. Goosie applies the escape-skip only in the `quote != 0` branch of the boundary scanners (internal/css/parser.go, parseRule's selector and declaration loops and parseBlockWithRules' statement loop), so outside a string the `'` of `\'` still opens one. Measured on a minimal file (one `.u{background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;...\'26\'...)}` rule plus `.after{background:#0f0}` and a text node, viewport 400x300): Chromium computes `.u` width 120px and `.after` rgb(0,255,0) - both rules survive; eef92ae paints 2,806 ink px (both boxes gone, only the text), and da68c5b paints 16,325 (both boxes). This is a REGRESSION introduced by a9f6218, which added the inside-string skip. Second measurement, on vnexpress.net's own second inline <style> block (94,344 bytes, one line, 80 single quotes, 409 backslashes) with a `.ZZ{background:#0f0;width:120px;height:120px}` marker appended: da68c5b paints the marker (14,400 px), eef92ae paints nothing (0 px). The two builds differ only in whether an escaped quote closes a string, so the old one was right by accident - an even number of quote characters leaves the state balanced - and the new one is wrong for that shape. Both directions are real: on the whole vnexpress.net page ink went 32 -> 320,348 between the da68c5b and eef92ae sweeps, because a different sheet on that page has the odd-count shape. Why no gate saw it: no test under test/css contains an escaped quote inside a string or a url token, and BR-186's nine tests cover the raw-newline and escaped-newline halves only; the render corpus has no escaped-quote-in-url fixture, so `make parity` is 83/83 green across this change. What closing needs: the escape-skip in both states at every boundary scanner (including the lenient sites that never end at a newline, parser.go:1321, :1346, :1419, :1681, :1784 and SplitDeclarations), expectations taken from Chromium measurement rather than memory, a unit oracle for `url(...\'...\')`, a parity fixture whose tail rule disappears when the scanner mis-tracks state, and a mutation proof that the fixture kills the current behaviour. CLOSED by e3b8292. Fix: `startsEscape` is tested before the quote branches in every quote-tracking scan (parseRule's selector and body loops, parseBlockWithRules' at-prelude, at-block, statement and nested-rule scans, ExpandSingleNestedSelector, SplitDeclarations), so an escaped byte is consumed with its backslash in both states; the body loop tracks parens apart from braces and 4.3.9 stops a quote inside `url(...)` from opening a string at all. Verified here, not claimed: five oracles green, `go test -count=1 ./...` rc 0, `go vet -all ./...` rc 0, `go test ./internal/archtest/` rc 0, `make parity` 84/84 at average 96.13% with css-features/10 at 97.42% and 0 blank bands, and the gate-level mutation - the same fixture rendered by eef92ae - scores 78.61% FAIL with 5 blank bands and parity exit 1. Re-measured outcomes on the inputs that opened this defect: the marker sheet (vnexpress style#1 + tail rule) paints 14,400 px again instead of 0, and the minimal probe recovers both boxes (16,325 px). Still open, deliberately not folded in: escape *decoding* (Goosie keeps the backslashes in the value while Chromium computes `url("data:x'y")`), hex escapes like `\A`, and selector matching on an escaped quote (GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001). None of them changes a pixel on the shapes measured here - Chromium computes `background-image: none` for the vnexpress-style URI too - so they stay recorded as debt rather than being fixed blind.

summary: A selector whose quoted value holds an escaped quote parses into the stylesheet but never matches, so the element keeps its unstyled box - the rule exists, the match does not.
evidence: GOOSIE-CSSSELECT-001. Measured 2026-10-26 on `.s[data-x="a\"b"]{background:#8e44ad;height:24px}` with `<div class="s" data-x='a"b'>`: Chromium computes the band 760x24 at rgb(142,68,173); Goosie paints no band at all. This is not the parser losing the rule - test/css/escaped_quote_test.go:TestEscapedQuoteInsideSelectorAttributeKeepsFollowingRules proves the rule and both its declarations survive (that half is BR-191) - so the loss is in selector matching, which still compares the raw text including the backslash. TASK-041 §7.6 already recorded 'selector text keeps the escape pair' as remaining debt; this is that debt with a measured page-level consequence. The render fixture css-features/10-escaped-quote-url.html deliberately uses an unescaped attribute value, so nothing in the corpus enshrines the wrong match. What closing needs: unescape the value when a selector is compiled (CSS Syntax L3 4.3.10 identifiers and 4.3.7 strings), one oracle per side (escaped quote, escaped space, hex escape like `\A`), and a fixture whose band only paints when the match works.

summary: visibility:hidden and element opacity never reach the display list, so boxes the author hid are painted anyway; once the CSS string fix let vnexpress's stylesheet through, one hidden full-width overlay turned the whole page into a flat grey panel.
evidence: GOOSIE-VIS-001. Measured on this host 2026-10-26 with cmd/dump-paint on a four-box document (/tmp/vis-probe2.html): the frozen display list is [EXTENT 800x200, FILL (0,0,800,200), FILL (8,8,108,58), FILL (8,58,108,108)] - the box carrying 'opacity:0;visibility:hidden' is emitted, the box carrying only 'visibility:hidden' is emitted, the box carrying only 'opacity:0' is emitted, and only the 'display:none' box is correctly absent. Pixels agree: a 400x300 render of the same overlay holds exactly 79,509 #f7f7f7 pixels in all four variants, i.e. the hidden and the transparent case are indistinguishable from the plain one. Code reading: internal/style/style.go:2559 stores cs.Visibility and the cascade keeps it in style_diff.go:101, but the only consumer in the tree is internal/paint/builder_controls.go:466 (list markers); no box or text path consults it. Opacity does have a raster consumer (internal/raster/tile.go applyOpacity) yet the value arriving for this element is opaque, so either the computed style never carries it into paint or paint builds the box without it - the implementer has to say which. PAGE-LEVEL CONSEQUENCE, and this is what makes it P1 rather than a missing feature: vnexpress's '.wrap-all-menu{width:100%;float:left;background:#f7f7f7;position:absolute;top:calc(100% + 10px);opacity:0;visibility:hidden}' used to be dropped along with the rest of its stylesheet. After GOOSIE-CSSSTRING-003 closed at e3b8292 the rule is admitted, so the sweep at 2ca7889 records the page as BLANK_OUTPUT (coverage 0.0, ink 32, doc_height 691) where the sweep at eef92ae recorded LOW_COVERAGE (coverage 0.441, ink 320,348, doc_height 1625). Attribution was measured on one saved copy of the page (254,146 characters, rendered both with and without its <script> blocks) across three binaries: eef92ae PNG 316,893 B / ink 261,030, 72a11f8 PNG 224,125 B / ink 261,030, 2ca7889 PNG 4,837 B / ink 345,600 - the script-free column is byte-identical between the first two, which rules out TASK-039's script execution as the cause and points at the newly admitted CSS. The fix is NOT the reason to revert: on the same nine vnexpress sheets the parser now yields 882 rules where the pre-fix parser yielded 174, and a 120x120 marker rule appended to the end of the 94 KB sheet survives on main (14,400 ink px) but is lost on the pre-fix binary (0). What closing needs: a hidden box produces no paint commands while still holding layout space, opacity applies to the element's own background, borders and text and composites its descendants, both are pinned by unit oracles at the style->paint boundary, and a parity fixture scored against Chromium plus the live vnexpress row moving back out of BLANK_OUTPUT. Registered from sweep 2026-10-25T1952Z-2ca78897. CLOSED by TASK-044 (merged 9e08c9d), re-measured by the integrator on this host, and registered as QC cases BR-195 / BR-196 / BR-197 in f1cb986. Every closing condition this entry asked for is met except one, and that one was the wrong condition: (a) a hidden box emits no paint commands while holding layout space - `test/paint/visibility_paint_test.go` 4 tests, and the integrator's mutation `visibilityHidden := false` fails `invisible_box_test.go:100` with two corner fills at `op=1`/`op=0.5` (rc 1); (b) opacity reaches the element's own background, borders and text and composites its descendants - `test/paint/opacity_paint_test.go` 5 tests; (c) unit oracles at the style->paint boundary - plus `test/style/opacity_visibility_computed_test.go` 2 tests, whose mutation (returning to `cs.Opacity = float32(parsed.Num)`) fails with the three distinct errors `#d = 5, want 1`, `#f = 50, want 0.5`, `#bad = 0, want 1`; (d) a parity fixture scored against Chromium - `css-features/12-hidden-and-transparent.html` 98.07% and `css-features/13-anonymous-group-opacity.html` 92.67%, corpus 87/87 average 96.14%, known gaps unchanged at 5 fixtures / 10 bands. (e) `vnexpress` moving out of BLANK_OUTPUT did NOT happen and was never caused only by this defect: TASK-044 §5.9 measured ink 0 -> 0 with only `doc_height` 706 -> 526, and the 216,000 `#f7f7f7` pixels are a legitimate `min-height:270px` header band, not the overlay - the page's remaining cause is content never being built (GOOSIE-LIVE-001) plus the corner ink now owned by GOOSIE-LIVE-006, so BLANK_OUTPUT is tracked there and not claimed as a closure here. Two residuals split out rather than left behind a green row: group compositing is still per-command (GOOSIE-COMPOSITE-001) and text/inline fragment boxes repaint their generating element's background (GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001); `visibility:collapse` is folded into `hidden` (GOOSIE-COLLAPSE-001) and `ContentVisibility` still has no consumer (GOOSIE-CONTENTVIS-001). The measured opacity of a *faded* box is also one declaration per element, not per generated box: anonymous blocks, anonymous table boxes and every text run copy the element's computed style verbatim (`s = *parent`, `cs := *parent`), so pass 1 of the same branch doubled the fade on the most common shape and the integrator's mutation reproduces it - `TestGroupOpacityCountedOncePerElement` red on exactly anon 0.25 / anondiv 0.25 / quarter 0.0625 / tableAnon 0.25, against Chromium min_lum 126 -> alpha 0.506 and 190 -> 0.255 measured on this host from freshly shot PNGs.

summary: The live sweep's FETCH_FAILED label is decided by Chromium's fetch rather than Goosie's, so a page Goosie did render is filed as a fetch failure and the row never says which side has no picture.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-007. testdata/live-parity.py:171 returns FETCH_FAILED straight from caps['fetch_error'], and :222 fills that key with the result of renderers.chromium(...); the same-iteration goosie_rc and doc_height are computed after it and never consulted by that branch. Measured on the five FETCH_FAILED rows of sweep 2026-10-25T1952Z-2ca78897: bbc.co.uk net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED with goosie rc 1; washingtonpost.com net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR with goosie rc 0 and doc_height 8654; cnn.com 'Timeout 30000ms exceeded' with rc 0 and doc_height 36511; aljazeera.com 'Timeout 30000ms exceeded' with rc 0 and doc_height 30362; moe.gov ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED with rc 1. Three of the five are Chromium-side failures on pages where Goosie produced a document, so the label describes the reference browser being unavailable, not the engine failing. Sweep 2026-10-25T2017Z-6071b8b9, run 25 minutes later with no engine change touching those sites, moved the label on its own: aljazeera.com FETCH_FAILED -> OK and straitstimes.com OK -> FETCH_FAILED. What closing needs: two labels (CHROMIUM_FETCH_FAILED against GOOSIE_FETCH_FAILED), or one label whose note names both sides, and the comparable-pages floor counted from whichever side is unusable so a Chromium outage is not silently read as an engine result. Sweep 2026-10-25T2045Z-ec0f7fb9, 28 minutes later: FETCH_FAILED went 5 -> 7 and the two additions are exactly the predicted signature - sggp.org.vn LOW_COVERAGE -> FETCH_FAILED and aljazeera.com OK -> FETCH_FAILED, each keeping a doc_height (16,067 and 30,362) that only the Goosie side can have produced, because that field comes from renderers.structure while the Chromium image is the one that failed. So an engine-correct row (sggp: coverage 0.471, pct 45.53) can be re-filed as a fetch failure by a later run, and aljazeera's 'OK' in sweep 4 was in fact pct_exact 1.2 (see GOOSIE-LIVE-004), which is why losing it says nothing about the engine. Same sweep also shows the noise floor is not a constant: its own repeated 12-site pass reports max |delta_pct_exact| 18.36 (vnexpress.net) where sweep 4 reported 3.45 for the same page and no label flipped in either.

summary: Nothing proves a wheel delta over the document scrolls it at browser level, and the one attempt to do so moved nothing in 30/30 runs, so the mouse-wheel path from the loop to the tab is unverified end to end.
evidence: GOOSIE-WHEEL-001. Measured 2026-10-26 on 6071b8b while replacing GOOSIE-FLAKE-002's second key press with a wheel step: injecting surface.Event{Kind: surface.EvScroll, Delta: frame.Point{Y:300}, Pos: frame.Point{X:300, Y:300}} into the headless e2e browser after tab 2's PageDown, then waiting for active.ScrollY() to advance past the keyboard offset, failed 30/30 runs under -race (diagnostics: journey_p1_tabs_test.go timed out, presents=409, injected=10) - the document never moved. The layers below do work: test/platform/headless_test.go:135 shows the window queueing a delta, test/surface/loop_test.go:96 shows the loop summing deltas across frames, and cmd/goosie/main_test.go:1168 asserts intercept() declines a wheel over content so it is forwarded rather than eaten by the tab strip. What is missing is the last hop: no test shows a forwarded delta reaching scrollContentTo or changing a tab's ScrollY, and cmd/goosie/toolbar_window.go:811 is where the forwarding decision is made. Not established which half is at fault - the injected event shape (no At, no Scale, content coordinates possibly in a different space) or the wiring itself; the 30/30 result is the measurement, not the verdict. What closing needs: one journey oracle 'a wheel down over the document increases the active tab's ScrollY, and switching tabs restores that offset', plus the same oracle for a delta arriving while the loop is drawing.

summary: TASK-037 fixed the value one option submits; four neighbouring surfaces still disagree with Chromium on the same markup: CSS option:checked resolves the first authored selection, the painted label is raw text content, option.label is unsupported, and JS option.value returns an empty string for a text-only option.
evidence: Split out of GOOSIE-FORMVALUE-001 when that closed, each half read in source and named rather than inferred. (a) Style/paint disagree with the selection: matchesPseudo (internal/css/selector.go:882-910) keeps `if c.HasAttribute("selected") && selected == nil` at :901, i.e. FIRST wins, while SelectedOption (internal/engine/focus.go:694) now takes the last - so `option:checked` styles the wrong option on two-authored-selection markup. (b) paintSelect (internal/paint/builder_controls.go:271-291) draws `c.TextContent()` with no normalisation, so the indented option an entire page uses paints its own newlines and indent, and its last-wins loop matches the engine but not (a). (c) option.label: Chromium's anchor prints label "  My Label  " for `<option label="  My Label  ">` while value falls back to text content; Goosie has no label attribute path at all (optionValue, internal/engine/focus.go:639). (d) JS DOM: __getValue__ (internal/js/js.go:809-823) returns the value attribute or "" - an `<option>` with only text answers `option.value === ""` in scripts, where Chromium answers the normalised text. (e) optgroup and multiple/size>1: selectOptionNodes and SelectedOption walk direct children only, so an option inside an `<optgroup>` stays unreachable (recorded at internal/engine/select.go:46-48) and a two-selected `multiple` control has no defined reading. Why it matters: BR-101 and BR-139 cannot be closed on the value fix alone, because both cases also name paint and announced name. Measured on this host 2026-10-26 at ec0f7fb.

summary: The accessibility tree has no heading role: the role vocabulary stops at 13 roles with nothing for h1-h6, so a page's structure - the thing a screen-reader user navigates by - is invisible, and catalogue case BR-139 cannot be closed as written.
evidence: BR-139 asks for 'role, name, value, href reflect the DOM' on a page with heading/link/button/input. grep -rn 'RoleHeading' internal/ test/ cmd/ returns nothing; the whole vocabulary is internal/ax/ax.go:11-24 (RoleDocument, Group, StaticText, Link, Button, Image, TextField, Search, ProgressBar, Meter, TabGroup, Tab, ComboBox, Option). A heading therefore arrives as RoleStaticText like any other paragraph, and no oracle exists to tag - the untagged AX tests cover link href (test/engine/accessibility_test.go:54), image alt (:68), button name (:79), input value (:87) and the document root (:32), but nothing asserts a heading. Registered while integrating TASK-037: the option label/value normalisation now traces BR-139, which is exactly the moment the row's remaining half became visible. Roadmap-v2 does not record this gap (its only accessibility line is :94, Find/selection/zoom indicator + 'verified by the accessibility tree'), so the row stays NOT RUN rather than DEFERRED. What closing needs: a heading role carrying its level, emitted by the AX builder, plus one oracle per BR-139 surface.

summary: A live sweep names its report after the commit that was HEAD when it finished, not the build whose pixels it measured, so a sweep that runs across a merge attributes reference-browser noise to engine commits that never ran.
evidence: Discovered while attributing sweep docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T2045Z-ec0f7fb9. run_id is built at report-write time: testdata/live-parity.py:694 calls _sha8(), which at :711-716 shells out to `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` - the pixels were captured 13 minutes earlier. Proof of the gap on this host: `make live-parity` depends on `build` (Makefile:68), and bin/goosie carries mtime 2026-10-25T20:31:52Z, the sweep start, while main moved through 0cefc1d (20:34:36Z), bcfab51 (20:37:59Z) and ec0f7fb (20:44:00Z) before the report was written at 20:45Z. So that report's rows describe the engine as of 6071b8b - the same sources the previous sweep 2026-10-25T2017Z-6071b8b9 measured, because the only commit in between (193de74, 20:33:16Z) touches docs/qa-live-parity and docs/qa-open-defects.json alone. Consequence read the right way: all four label flips between the two sweeps (sggp.org.vn LOW_COVERAGE -> FETCH_FAILED, aljazeera.com OK -> FETCH_FAILED, thanhnien.vn MISSING_REGIONS -> LOW_COVERAGE, nike.com MISSING_REGIONS -> OK) and the noise-floor jump (its own repeated 12-site pass: max |delta_pct_exact| 3.45 in sweep 4, 18.36 in sweep 5, on vnexpress.net, no label flipped in either) happened with identical engine code, so none of them is an engine result - which is exactly what GOOSIE-LIVE-004 and GOOSIE-LIVE-007 predict. What closing needs: name the report by the built binary (record `git rev-parse HEAD` at build time, or hash the binary itself into the JSON), and say so in the header line the reader sees first. CLOSED by TASK-045, re-measured by the integrator on this host before the merge (ca39672): capture_build() now runs at the start of the sweep, before the first page is fetched, and records the source SHA (full and short) plus the binary path and its SHA-256; the report file name and the JSON run_id are derived from that snapshot (`report_sha8`), never from write-time HEAD. Proofs run here, not read from the branch report: `python3 testdata/live-parity.py --selftest` exits 0 with 49 PASS, including a check that an unreadable binary is recorded as unhashed rather than guessed; deleting the JSON `build` key (testdata/live-parity.py:503) exits 1 with two checks red ('the JSON names the source SHA, the binary path and the binary SHA-256 - null', and the markdown first-lines check reporting UNKNOWN); a real 8-URL sweep against a freshly built binary wrote 2026-10-25T2145Z-0514d6d7.md whose first line names source `0514d6d7` and binary SHA-256 `79784739169147783f130d2fe320e87fac99d34a19af47ef66dc48f681b4719f`, and the JSON gained exactly one top-level key (`build`) with nothing removed. Regression the branch caused and disclosed itself: folding the SHA-8 helper into `_git_rev(abbrev)` dropped the `HEAD` argument, so a real sweep printed `source UNKNOWN` and named the file `-unknown.md`; that is now gated by three selftest checks. Reads on the record: sweeps #1-#5 keep their write-time names and must be interpreted through this entry's evidence rather than re-baselined, and sweep #6 onward is the first series whose attribution to a build is trustworthy. REOPENED by the integrator on 2026-10-26, and my own closure claim is withdrawn in this entry rather than quietly edited away. Sweep `docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb` is the counter-example: its `run_id` and filename end in `4302e3cb` — HEAD when the report was WRITTEN — while `build.source_sha8` in the same JSON says `9754fda4`, the build that produced the pixels. summary: Group opacity is multiplied per command at tile-raster time instead of compositing the faded group once offscreen, so two translucent layers sharing one `opacity` group darken twice.
evidence: GOOSIE-COMPOSITE-001 - disclosed by TASK-044 §5.9 and measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 (`/tmp/t46-check/group.html`, 300x120 DPR 1: a container with `opacity:0.5` holding two `rgba(0,0,255,0.5)` 60x60 boxes overlapping by 30 px). Single-box pixel agrees with Chromium exactly: goosie (191,191,255) vs chromium (191,191,255). The overlap does not: goosie (143,143,255) vs chromium (158,158,255), i.e. 0.25 applied twice (effective 0.4375) where the spec asks for 0.75 composited inside the group and the group once at 0.5 (effective 0.375). Root: `internal/raster/tile.go` reads `DisplayCmd.Opacity` per command, so nothing in the engine ever holds a group buffer; TASK-044 fixed which commands exist and what alpha each carries, not how they are combined. Blast radius: only visible when two translucent paintings overlap inside one faded group - non-overlapping boxes and non-faded groups agree with Chromium, which is why the parity corpus (87/87, average 96.14%) does not catch it and no fixture of mine is scored on it. What closing needs: an offscreen group buffer (or equivalent per-group composite) at the tile raster, a fixture whose overlap region is scored against Chromium, and the oracle extended to assert the overlap pixel rather than only the command alphas.

summary: Text-run and inline-fragment boxes repaint their generating element's background, so a translucent block background is composited again wherever a word sits.
evidence: GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001 - measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while reviewing TASK-044 §5.10, which names the same shape as out of scope. `cmd/dump-paint` on a 300x60 block with `background:rgb(200,0,0)` and the text `one two three four` emits the block fill `(0,0,300,60)` once and then one more fill per word box: `(0,0,24,18) (23,0,28,18) (27,0,52,18) (51,0,56,18) (55,0,88,18) (87,0,92,18) (91,0,118,18)`. With an opaque background the duplication is invisible (red over red), so it was never a paint-correctness bug until opacity/translucency arrived: with `background:rgba(200,0,0,0.5)` the same document renders (213,63,63) inside a word box against (227,127,127) elsewhere in the block, and Chromium renders (227,127,127) uniformly at all three sampled points - i.e. Goosie applies the element's own 0.5 alpha twice wherever a text fragment covers it. Inline *fragmenting* (one background per line fragment of an inline box) is correct CSS; what is wrong is a **block** element's background being re-emitted by the text runs layout splices under it, which is the same verbatim style copy that made group opacity double-count (`style.inheritStyle: cs := *parent`). TASK-044 deliberately kept translucent backgrounds out of faded groups in fixture 13 so the corpus would not score this. What closing needs: the fragment fills to carry the fragment's own background only, an oracle at the style->paint boundary asserting one background per box per line, and a scored fixture with a translucent block background over text. CORRECTION by the integrator, 2026-10-26: the fill list above first said six duplicate run fills; the true number is **seven** - `(91,0,118,18)` for the fourth word was left out of my own transcription. TASK-048's mutation-A log quotes all eight fills (one box + seven runs) and is the citation for the corrected list.
