summary: `visibility: collapse` is treated as `hidden`, so a table row or column that should collapse keeps its box and its share of the table grid.
evidence: GOOSIE-COLLAPSE-001 - registered from TASK-044 §5.9, which ships the simplification and says so in the code comment at `internal/paint/builder_box.go` ("`collapse` is treated as hidden here; table-part collapse is out of scope"). Per CSS 2.1 / UI, `collapse` on a row, rowgroup or column removes it from the table's width/height distribution (adjacent borders and half-borders merge), which is observably different from `hidden`; a box that only stops painting still occupies its cells. **Integrator note on evidence quality: not measured by me** - no Chromium anchor for a collapsed row exists in this repo and no oracle asserts either behaviour, so the size of the gap is unquantified. Priority P3 for that reason, not because the difference is small. What closing needs: a Chromium-measured collapsed-row fixture, then a decision on whether to implement table-part collapse or record it as out of scope for the release with the roadmap item named.

summary: `content-visibility: auto` resolves to no behaviour: only the literal `hidden` is consulted in layout and paint, so `auto` falls through to normal painting and sizing.
evidence: GOOSIE-CONTENTVIS-001 - registered while reviewing TASK-044 §5.9, which leaves the property alone deliberately. Scope of the claim, narrowed after checking the code: the property is **not** inert. `internal/style/style.go:2577` stores it, `DefaultStyle()` gives `visible` at :689, and there are real consumers - `internal/layout/block.go:240` and :2436 (`hidden` skips contents and can size from `ContainIntrinsicHeight`) and `internal/paint/builder_box.go:83` (`hidden` stops the subtree walk) - plus tests `test/style/content_visibility_test.go:TestContentVisibilityProperties`, `TestContentVisibilitySingleIntrinsicSize` and `test/layout/anchor_test.go:TestContentVisibilityHiddenLayoutSizing`. What is missing is `auto`: every comparison in the tree is `== "hidden"`, so the value the cascade stores for `auto` is read nowhere and a document using `content-visibility: auto` behaves as if it said `visible`. **Correction kept on the record: the first draft of this entry, written before the grep above, said the field had no consumer and no test. That was false and is withdrawn here rather than quietly edited away.** Not measured against Chromium on this host, so no claim is made about which part of the `auto` contract (skipped rendering, contain-intrinsic-size swap, finding-in-page) matters most. What closing needs: a Chromium anchor for `auto` on a long page, then either the behaviour or an explicit scope statement in the roadmap.

summary: An anonymous block box re-composites its generating block’s gradient or background-image, because `style.AnonymousBlockStyle` zeroes only `BackgroundColor` while `AnonymousTableStyle` zeroes all four background layers.
evidence: GOOSIE-ANONBG-001 - found by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while checking whether TASK-048’s new predicate (`internal/paint/builder_box.go:65 fragmentOwnsBackground`) left a hole at `obj.Node == nil -> true`, which is exactly the branch an anonymous block takes. Measured on `/tmp/t48-check/anon-grad.html` (a 300x76 block with `background:linear-gradient(rgba(200,0,0,.5),rgba(200,0,0,.5))` holding raw text plus a block sibling, so `cmd/dump-layout` shows anonymous boxes ID=11 (0,0,300,18) and ID=12 (0,38,300,18)), 400x120 DPR 1, counts over the box area: Chromium 13,370 px (227,127,127) + 8,595 px (228,127,127) and no doubled colour at all; main 12,000 px (227,127,127) + 8,190 px (213,63,63) doubled + 1,777 px (206,31,31) tripled; after TASK-048 12,000 px (227,127,127) + 10,026 px (213,63,63). The tripled colour disappears because it came from text runs (BR-198); the doubled band survives because it comes from the anonymous boxes, which own no background colour to zero — style.go:610 clears `BackgroundColor` only, while :635-642 (table) clears `BackgroundColor`, `BackgroundImage`, `BackgroundGradient` and `BackgroundRadialGradient`. So the mechanism TASK-048 added is right and the style layer is the one that is inconsistent. The solid-colour path is provably unreachable for anonymous boxes: `anon-bg.html` emits exactly one fill of `1677721728` post-fix against 8 on main, and dump-paint shows no anonymous-box-width fill in either build. Why the corpus does not catch it: fixture 13 keeps gradients out of translucent groups and fixture 14 uses a solid background. What closing needs: mirror :636-642 into `AnonymousBlockStyle` (or gate gradient/image paints on the same owner test in the builder), a fixture whose gradient band sits behind raw text beside a block sibling, and an oracle asserting one gradient fill per element. Not fixed here; needs a task.

summary: A `box-shadow` declaration is emitted once per text-run box as well as once per element, so translucent shadows stack inside the generating box; TASK-048 left this path ungated on purpose.
evidence: GOOSIE-SHADOWRUN-001 - reported by TASK-048 §6.2 and re-measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 on my own document `/tmp/t48-res/shadow.html` (a 300x60 block with `margin:10px`, `background:rgba(200,0,0,.5)` and `box-shadow:2px 2px 4px 1px rgba(0,0,200,.5)` holding `one two three four`). `cmd/dump-paint | grep -c color=25728` = **64** fills on main and **64** on the TASK-048 branch: 8 strips for the element’s own box plus 8 per text run over 7 runs — one declared shadow, sixty-four fills. `25728 = 0x00006480` is `rgba(0,0,200,.5)` premultiplied, so every one of them is the same declaration. Because a run’s rect lies inside the block’s padding area, the duplication is a colour error, not only wasted work: over the block region at DPR 1, Goosie holds 2,045 px (95,95,220), 972 px (127,127,227), 635 px (85,47,172) and 333 px (113,63,163) where Chromium holds (224,224,248) and (227,127,127); first contaminated pixel at (32,10) reads (85,47,172) against Chromium’s (227,127,127) — the same double-composite colour family as GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001. Root: `paintBoxShadow` sits behind `paintsInlineFragments` (`internal/paint/builder_box.go:114` in the pre-fix file) and TASK-048 deliberately gated only the four background layers, so text runs keep calling it. Separate and NOT part of this defect: at a point outside the box where Chromium has already faded its blur, Goosie reads (95,95,220) against (247,247,253) — a shadow-strength/blur-model question owned by `paintBoxShadow`, unchanged by anything here. What closing needs: one shadow per element box (fragments excluded the same way backgrounds are), a pinned command-count oracle (TASK-048’s `inline_background_repaint_test.go` is the template), and a scored fixture with a translucent shadow behind text. Needs a task.

summary: An inline element’s border is never painted at all: `paintBorders` sits behind a non-inline test, so inline boxes lose their borders instead of fragmenting them per line.
evidence: GOOSIE-INLINEBORDER-001 - reported by TASK-048 §6.1 and re-measured independently by the integrator on 2026-10-26 on my own document `/tmp/t48-res/inlineborder.html` (`div{width:300px;height:60px;margin:10px;background:rgba(200,0,0,.5)}` with `span{border:3px solid rgba(0,0,200,.5)}` around "two"). `cmd/dump-paint` emits **0** BORDER commands on main and **0** on the TASK-048 branch — the only BORDER in the engine’s output for a block border test appears for the block itself (`BORDER rect=(0,0,306,66)` in TASK-048’s §6.1 dump), never for an inline. Chromium paints the span’s border box: over my measured region Chromium holds 198 px of (113,63,163) — exactly `rgba(0,0,200,.5)` composited once over the block tint (227,127,127) — and Goosie holds none of that colour anywhere; Goosie’s only extra colours in the region are glyph antialiasing (125,70,70 / 68,38,38 / 191,107,107). Root is the same test that protects borders from the duplication in GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001: `paintBoxDecoration` runs `paintBorders` only when `computed.Display != style.DisplayInline`, so text runs (inline) cannot re-emit the element’s border — which is why no border duplication exists to register — but an inline element’s own border is dropped rather than fragmented one box per line, as CSS fragmentation requires. Blast radius: any page that draws a rule or a chip outline with `border` on an inline element (including `<a>`/`<abbr>`/`<code>` styling) loses it silently; invisible to the corpus because no fixture puts a border on an inline box. What closing needs: emit one border per inline fragment of an inline element (left/right strips only at the true start/end of the run, per css-text-decor L3 §4.6 analogue), an oracle counting BORDER commands per fragment, and a scored fixture. Needs a task.

summary: A live-sweep row is not reproducible even when the binary is bit-identical: what a page’s row records depends on how far that page’s own scripts got at capture time, so the same URL on the same engine yields a 4,368 px document in one sweep and a 34,795 px one in the next.
evidence: GOOSIE-LIVE-009 - measured by the integrator on 2026-10-26 while attributing sweep 7 (`docs/qa-live-parity/2026-10-26T0011Z-741fdd37`, build source `741fdd37`) against sweep 6 (`2026-10-25T2212Z-4302e3cb`, build source `9754fda4`). The engine side is provably deterministic: three consecutive `./bin/goosie -backend headless -width 1280 -height 1024 -dpr 1 -screenshot -url https://www.walmart.com/` runs on this host produced **one** PNG hash (`6472fedefe08…`, 500,177 B) and **one** ink count (1,138,344 non-white px) with rc 0 and the same stderr each time. Yet walmart’s row says `ink_goosie` 1,077,200 with `doc_height` 4,368 in sweep 6 and 519,333 with `doc_height` 34,795 in sweep 7 — an 8× document height and a 52% ink swing on a URL whose HTML is byte-stable (three `curl` fetches: 450,325 B, sha256 prefix `14b086e65f377ad7`, identical). The page’s own script state, not the engine and not the HTML, is what moved. Scale of it, from the same two sweeps: **84 of 94** compared rows have byte-identical `ink_goosie` across two different builds, and every row where both `ink_goosie` and `ink_chromium` are identical also has `pct_exact` delta **exactly 0.00** (apnews.com, datatracker.ietf.org, doc.rust-lang.org/book and std, docs.kernel.org, docs.python.org ×3, en.wikipedia ×3 …) — so the metric is reproducible and the noise is entirely in what the reference and the page contribute at capture time. The movers confirm the direction: nld.com.vn `pct_exact` −27.39 with `ink_goosie` −0.1% and `ink_chromium` **+391%**; de.wikipedia −6.08 with ink Goosie identical and Chromium +42%; zingnews `ink_goosie` **+68.8%** (an engine change that only *removes* fills cannot add ink, so this is page state); two of six label flips (de/zh.wikipedia) happen with Goosie’s ink identical to the byte. Consequence for how a sweep may be read: a label flip or a `pct_exact` move is an engine result only when the engine’s own numbers moved too — which is why sweep 7 attributes exactly **one** of its six flips to code (see GOOSIE-INLINEBG-001’s note) and the rest to capture state. Not the same defect: GOOSIE-LIVE-004 (a row can read OK while the pixels are nowhere near each other), GOOSIE-LIVE-007 (FETCH_FAILED is decided on Chromium’s side — sweep 7 proves it again with bestbuy.com’s `TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms`, where Goosie never got a turn), GOOSIE-LIVE-008 (report naming). What closing needs: pin the page state the row is allowed to depend on (wait for network idle plus a settled script-error count, or capture `doc_height` twice and refuse to score an unstable page), and record which of the two the row was taken with. Needs a task. Sweep 7 also brought its own repeated-pass noise floor back tighter than sweep 5/6 had it: 12 sites, 10 comparable, max |delta_pct_exact| **0.67**, max |delta_coverage| 0.077, **0** label flips. Read together that is the point of this entry - the spread on *static* pages is well under a point, while the pages that moved between sweeps moved 6 to 27 points, and every one of those movers has a reference- or script-side number that moved with it. A sweep's own repeated pass therefore cannot detect the instability this entry describes: it re-renders the same pages inside one capture window, where the page state is already fixed.
